answer: Threshold FHE lets a group run arbitrary computations on encrypted data and decrypt only the final result, and the delta of the design is that the secret key is shared so no party can decrypt intermediate values. The vertex of the protocol is that the computation itself is public while the inputs stay encrypted, so anyone can audit the circuit. A Sybil cannot learn honest users' data from the computation, and a gale of fake inputs is caught because the circuit enforces one credential per verified identity.
